title: Fppf quotient comparison for restriction of an equivalence relation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $V,R$ be $S$-schemes. An equivalence relation $(s,t):R\to V\times_SV$ [def-pc-fibre-product] means that for every $S$-scheme $T$ the map on sections is injective and identifies $R(T)$ with an equivalence relation on $V(T)$. Let $g:A\to V$ be any morphism of $S$-schemes and let $R_A=A\times_{g,V,t}R\times_{s,V,g}A$ be the restricted equivalence relation, with projections $(a,r,b)\mapsto b,a$. Write $V/R$ and $A/R_A$ for the sheafifications [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of their sectionwise quotient presheaves on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site] of $S$. The canonical morphism $A/R_A\to V/R$ is a monomorphism of sheaves. If $h_A=s\circ\operatorname{pr}_R:A\times_{g,V,t}R\to V$ is surjective, flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], that canonical morphism is an isomorphism. All schemes and fibre products are taken in the chosen site bound.

proof.text: Write $P(T)=V(T)/R(T)$ and $P_A(T)=A(T)/R_A(T)$. By the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], $R_A(T)$ consists exactly of triples $(a,r,b)$ with $g a=t r$ and $s r=g b$. Thus $a$ and $b$ are related exactly when $g a$ and $g b$ are related in $V(T)$; symmetry allows either order. Reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity follow from those of $R(T)$, and uniqueness of $r$ for its endpoints gives injectivity into $A(T)^2$. The function $v_T:P_A(T)\to P(T)$ sending $[a]$ to $[g a]$ is well-defined and injective: equality of its values is precisely the relation just described. Restrictions preserve these triples, so the quotients and $v$ are presheaves and a natural transformation.

Put $F=P^\#$ and $F_A=P_A^\#$ with units $\eta$ and $\eta_A$. The sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] applied to $\eta v:P_A\to F$ gives a unique sheaf morphism $\alpha:F_A\to F$ with $\alpha\eta_A=\eta v$. In particular $\alpha(\eta_A[a])=\eta[g a]$. This is the canonical morphism in the statement.

For $x,y\in F_A(T)$ with $\alpha(x)=\alpha(y)$, the local-representative clause of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] and [lem-weil-pbc-site-coverings-common-refinement] give one fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ and $p_i,q_i\in P_A(T_i)$ representing $x|_{T_i},y|_{T_i}$. Step 2 gives $\eta(v(p_i))=\eta(v(q_i))$. The local-equality clause of the same local-sections node, now applied to $P$, gives coverings of each $T_i$ on which these two presheaf sections agree. Step 1's injection and naturality of $v$ make $p_i$ and $q_i$ equal on those refinements. The composition axiom and the uniqueness part of the sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] imply $x=y$. Thus every $\alpha_T$ is injective. If two sheaf morphisms into $F_A$ have equal composites with $\alpha$, evaluating at every $T$ and cancelling $\alpha_T$ makes their components equal. Therefore $\alpha$ is a monomorphism.

Assume $h:E=A\times_{g,V,t}R\to V$, $h=s\operatorname{pr}_R$, is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Then $\{h\}$ is an fppf covering by [def-pc-fppf-site]. For $z\in F(T)$, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] gives an fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ and classes $c_i\in P(T_i)$ representing $z|_{T_i}$. Choose representatives $f_i:T_i\to V$ of $c_i$. Pull back the covering $\{h\}$ along $f_i$: the site pullback axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] gives singleton coverings $p_i:W_i=T_i\times_{f_i,V,h}E\to T_i$, whose composites cover $T$. The other projection supplies $a_i:W_i\to A$ and $r_i:W_i\to R$, satisfying $g a_i=t r_i$ and $s r_i=f_i p_i$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Hence $[g a_i]=[f_i p_i]$ in $P(W_i)$, and Step 2 yields $\alpha(\eta_A[a_i])=z|_{W_i}$. All these pullbacks are in the chosen site bound. No property of $g$ beyond being an $S$-morphism has been used.

proof.text: The sections $w_i=\eta_A[a_i]\in F_A(W_i)$ of Step 4 agree on every $W_i\times_TW_j$: their $\alpha$-images are both the restriction of $z$, so Step 3 gives equality. The sheaf equalizer condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] glues them uniquely to $w\in F_A(T)$. Since $\alpha(w)$ and $z$ agree on the covering, the same uniqueness condition gives $\alpha(w)=z$. Together with Step 3 this proves $\alpha_T$ bijective for every $T$. Define $\beta_T(z)$ to be its unique inverse image. For $u:T'\to T$, naturality gives $\alpha_{T'}(\beta_T(z)|_{T'})=z|_{T'}=\alpha_{T'}(\beta_{T'}(z|_{T'}))$; Step 3 cancels $\alpha_{T'}$, proving naturality of $\beta$. The two inverse equations hold componentwise by uniqueness. Thus $\beta$ is a sheaf inverse of $\alpha$, proving the isomorphism clause.

Step 5: overlap agreement via Step 3, gluing, and a natural inverse. The cited statements say what each step takes from them. Edge cases (g=id, V empty, A empty, diagonal R, full relation with non-flat g) are consistent. lean.statement: theorem relation_restriction_quotient {S : Scheme.{u}} {R V A : Over S} (s t : R ⟶ V) [Mono (prod.lift s t)] (hrel : ∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ V ↦ ∃ r : T ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a ∧ r ≫ t = b)) (g : A ⟶ V) (F : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (η : coequalizer (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ⟶ F.obj) (hη : ∀ G : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun k : F.obj ⟶ G.obj ↦ η ≫ k)) (F' : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (η' : coequalizer (yoneda.map (pullback.snd (pullback.snd g t ≫ s) g)) (yoneda.map (pullback.fst (pullback.snd g t ≫ s) g ≫ pullback.fst g t)) ⟶ F'.obj) (hη' : ∀ G : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun k : F'.obj ⟶ G.obj ↦ η' ≫ k)) : ∃ α : F' ⟶ F, (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map (pullback.snd (pullback.snd g t ≫ s) g)) (yoneda.map (pullback.fst (pullback.snd g t ≫ s) g ≫ pullback.fst g t)) ≫ η') ≫ α.hom = yoneda.map g ≫ (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ≫ η) ∧ Mono α ∧ (Surjective (pullback.snd g t ≫ s).left → Flat (pullback.snd g t ≫ s).left → LocallyOfFinitePresentation (pullback.snd g t ≫ s).left → IsIso α)
